analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The changed range is head lines 1561-1569, a new paragraph about byte-fallback token decoding: LocalTokenizerBridge.decode releases a trailing run of `<0xHH>` tokens, and DetokenizerV2 holds back U+FFFD. That range is not inside the two supplied units, which show surrounding head text at lines 3593-4003 and 4004-4073. The supplied units are unchanged context, so the diff itself could not be examined line by line beyond the patch excerpt.

The documented behavior has no visible security impact. It concerns output text correctness for Gemma 4 and affects neither crypto, authorization, attestation nor key custody. It also does not touch the prefix-cache or SSD paths (T-041), the coordinator-to-provider transport (TB-002), or the MLX engine boundary (TB-007). Plaintext handling is unchanged: decoded text still flows through the existing encrypt-before-send path (T-008). The docs describe no new file writes, temp files or network behavior.

I examined the surrounding head text in the units: link-probe and share-probe history files, tensor-parallel notes, and prefix cache scoping. This text is unchanged context and describes pre-existing behavior. I raised no findings on it, because changes there are not shown. Remaining uncertainty: the actual Swift change to LocalTokenizerLoader.swift is outside the supplied evidence. If that source was changed in the same PR, a later pass should check the decoder for unbounded buffering or loops on adversarial token streams. Consumers can influence generated tokens, but the model output is bounded by the existing length limits.
